items.q: I have a new car. Should I get it detailed before I start using it?
items.a: Yes, new cars rarely leave the dealer in the condition they should be in. Transportation film residue, compound dust from the dealer's prep, contamination from outdoor storage near ports and rail depots, all of these affect the paint before it reaches you. A new car detail corrects the paint and applies protection from day one, before the car accumulates any driving history on its finish.

items.q: What is paint correction?
items.a:
Paint correction is the process of removing defects from the surface of the paint, swirl marks, fine scratches, water etching, oxidation and surface haze, by carefully levelling the clear coat using machine polishing. Done correctly, it restores the paint to a depth and clarity that makes the car look better than it did from the factory.

At Miracle Detail, every correction job begins with a full assessment using a paint depth gauge, a £4,000 gloss and orange peel measurement instrument, and a digital microscope, so Paul understands exactly what the paint can give before a pad touches it.

items.q: My car has swirl marks. Can they all be removed?
items.a: In most cases, yes, or very close to it. The level of correction achievable depends on the thickness of the clear coat and how deep the defects go. Paul's five-level correction system ranges from enhancement polish (up to 65-75% defect removal) through to concours-level correction (100%). He will assess the paint and tell you honestly what's achievable before any work begins.

items.q: Why has my black car developed swirl marks after washing?
items.a:
Almost always because incorrect washing technique or the wrong products were used, either by the owner, a previous owner or a valet. Dark colours, especially black, show swirl marks and fine scratches more dramatically than light colours because the marks reflect light at visible angles.

Swirls that appear after a wash are often pre-existing, the polish or glaze that was masking them has been washed away, revealing what was underneath. Paint correction removes the defects permanently. The aftercare washing guide explains how to prevent them recurring.

items.q: Does paint correction remove deep scratches?
items.a: It depends on the depth. Scratches in the clear coat, which represents the vast majority of surface damage, can be corrected by machine polishing. Scratches that have broken through the clear coat and into the base coat or primer cannot be corrected by polishing and require paint repair. Paul will assess and advise honestly on what's possible and, where repair is needed, can coordinate bodyshop work accordingly.

items.q: What does a ceramic coating actually do?
items.a: A ceramic coating is a semi-permanent protective layer that bonds to the paint's surface. It provides protection against UV damage, chemical contamination, bird lime, water etching and environmental fallout, while delivering a depth of gloss that no wax or sealant can match. It also makes the car significantly easier to wash, as contamination doesn't bond to the coated surface the way it does to bare paint.

items.q: Why does it matter who applies the coating?
items.a: A ceramic coating is only as good as the preparation beneath it. Applied over contaminated or uncorrected paint, the coating locks the problems in, permanently. Applied incorrectly, it underperforms from day one. Paul is Feynlab's only global ambassador and the detailer who co-developed Ceramic by Paul Dalton. He knows the chemistry as well as anyone applying it. The application matters just as much as the product.

items.q: Which Feynlab coating is right for my car?
items.a: It depends on how you use the car, how long you want the protection to last and whether self-healing is a priority. The Feynlab range runs from the 1-2 year Original Ceramic through to the 7-year Self-Heal Plus, Paul's own Ceramic by Paul Dalton sits at 3 years and is the most popular choice. Paul will recommend the right product for your car and your requirements, there's no pressure to go for the most expensive option if it isn't what the car needs.

items.q: Does a ceramic coating mean I never need to wash the car?
items.a: No, but it makes washing significantly easier and less frequent. The coating's hydrophobic properties mean water and contamination bead and release rather than bonding to the surface. Regular washing with the correct products is still required. See the aftercare guide for Paul's full recommended procedure and product list.

items.q: What is PPF and how is it different to ceramic coating?
items.a:
Paint Protection Film is a physical urethane film applied directly to the painted surface. It absorbs stone chips, resists abrasion and protects against the kind of physical impact that ceramic coating cannot prevent. Ceramic coating is a chemical barrier, strong for chemical protection, UV resistance and gloss enhancement, but it won't stop a stone chip.

The two are complementary. Many clients have PPF applied to the high-impact zones, bonnet, bumper, wings, with ceramic coating over the entire car. Paul will advise on the best approach for your car and how you use it.

items.q: How long has Paul been installing PPF?
items.a: Since 2006, longer than any other detailer in the UK. Nearly two decades of experience fitting film to everything from daily drivers to Bugattis and Koenigseggs.

items.q: Can PPF be removed?
items.a: Yes. PPF is designed to be removable, including colour change films, without damaging the original paint beneath, provided the paint was in good condition when the film was applied. This is one of the major advantages over a permanent colour respray.

items.q: Do you offer matte PPF?
items.a: Yes, gloss, matte and colour PPF are all available. Matte PPF protects existing matte or satin finishes, and can also be used to convert a gloss car to a matte appearance. Colour PPF allows a complete colour change while keeping the original paint beneath fully protected and reversible.

items.q: What is dry ice cleaning?
items.a:
Dry ice cleaning uses solid CO2 pellets at -78.5°C, accelerated at high speed onto the surface being cleaned. Three things happen simultaneously, kinetic impact dislodges contamination, the extreme cold causes it to contract and fracture away, and the dry ice converts directly from solid to gas, leaving zero moisture and zero residue. No water, no chemicals, no risk to wiring or electronics.

Paul was the first detailer in the UK to use dry ice cleaning, in 2014. He has been using the technology for over a decade while much of the industry is still catching up.

items.q: Is dry ice cleaning safe for engine bays and electronics?
items.a: Yes, this is one of its biggest advantages over steam or pressure washing. Because the dry ice converts directly to gas with no liquid phase, there is no moisture introduced to the surface. Wiring, connectors, sensors and electronic components are completely safe. It can clean areas that steam or water cannot safely reach.
